messages:
Ivy (People Ops): Quick policy note: two small clarifications launching now based on feedback 1) Carryover Exception: managers can approve a one-time PTO carryover up to 3 days for employees with documented operational constraints (e.g., critical launches). People Ops must be CC'd. 2) Travel Safety Checklist: if you're traveling internationally for urgent work, you must complete the 2-min travel safety checklist before booking to streamline Security checks. Links: https://redwood.company/hr/carryover-exception and https://redwood.company/hr/travel-safety :sparkles:
Noah (Eng): Nice. Is the carryover visible in payroll or is it a manual adjustment?
Sam (Finance): It's a manual adjustment triggered by People Ops after manager approval; it'll appear as "Carryover Exception" on the payslip. We'll include a flag in monthly exports for audits.
Aisha (Sales): For the travel checklist, what if Security needs extra time? We often book same-day.
Ivy (People Ops): The checklist flags urgent requests to Security; for truly same-day travel, include the incident/customer link and Security will prioritize within 4 hours. If formal approval can't be obtained in time, proceed only if legal entry requirements are met.
Compliance Bot: Reminder: incomplete travel checklist entries will default to manual review and can delay reimbursements.
Noah (Eng): Retroactive carryover? Someone missed filing last sprint.
Ivy (People Ops): Managers can retro-approve within 10 days of the period. After that People Ops review required. DM me with the incident link if urgent.
Aisha (Sales): Thanks Ivy, this should help with last-minute sales trips.
Ivy (People Ops): Thanks all. We'll monitor usage for 60 days and tweak as needed. Post questions in #people-ops or DM. :thumbsup:
